maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
A school teacher with
$400,000 to buy shares; boy!

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
My hon. friend was once a school teacher, but he has not done quite so well. I have not noticed any great monuments to him about Canada. I have read a great deal about him in Hansard, but no great accomplishments were mentioned.
Well now, that was the situation gentlemen. Make of it what you will. We will talk about it on the hustings. I will talk about this great Canadian project and the opposition it has encountered at all stages, particularly the battle in this house and the picayune attacks that are being made by two opposition parties. Then the opposition can tell the electors how much trouble they were able to create in the House of Commons, and we will let the voters decide. I think that is probably the best way to settle this argument. In the meantime, the transaction is what it is. I have explained it as it appears
Trans-Canada Pipe Lines to me. If anyone else wants to do any tearing down of reputations, let him stand up and go to it.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
I feel that there are a few things that should be said today. I realize, of course, that this is the hunting season, and the fact that we are expecting a general election some time might, in itself, account for the bombastic oratory we have heard today. I would not look for anything else, of course. The two parties to my right are trying to wring out of the Trans-Canada Pipe Line controversy every drop they can possibly get that will help them in their losing battle.
However, I was surprised to see the Leader of the Opposition (Mr. Diefenbaker) stand up in this house and talk about buccaneers; about facts concealed; about how we now know the reason for the rush to force the bill through parliament; about the promoters of the company, including Mr. Tanner and Mr. Coates, having risked nothing but their signatures and reaped fabulous profits. I have said on former occasions that there seem to be two kinds of socialism in this country, one being promoted by the C.C.F. and the other by the Conservatives. The Conservative brand is not, it seems to me, nearly as down to earth as the other. I want to say, Mr. Speaker, that a lot of the stuff that has been spoken here this afternoon is sheer hypocrisy.
For a time last spring, as has already been pointed out, all that the Conservatives could do in this house was advocate that Frank McMahon and his company be the alternative to the Trans-Canada Pipe Line Company and given the opportunity to build this pipe line. At the time, I thought if the Conservatives knew anything about Frank McMahon and what he had made out of transmission companies they would probably be somewhat red in the face. It was interesting this afternoon to hear them talk about buccaneers in the light of the stand the Conservatives took a year ago.
I did not rise to defend anybody this afternoon except a man whom I consider to be a great Canadian. I was raised with him and I went to school with him. I am speaking now of Nathan Tanner, and I know something about his background. I know something about his success. I sat in the cabinet of Alberta with him for eight years, and I know something that was withheld today, whether or not deliberately I am not saying, but it was withheld. The hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre (Mr. Knowles) was very careful to point out and emphasize that Mr. Tanner was a school teacher prior
1614	HOUSE OF
Trans-Canada Pipe Lines to entering the Alberta cabinet. He emphasized that on two or three different occasions, and the fact he was a member of the Social Credit government, implying there was something immoral, something wrong, some departure from principle. In fact, Mr. Tanner has made a success of things in the field of business, as well as an outstanding success in the field of government.
Let me just point out the thing the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre withheld from this house, and when he talks about guilt for withholding I think he should take a good look in the mirror. Here is something he did not take the trouble to find out. It is true Mr. Tanner was a school principal but everyone in southern Alberta who knew him also knew him as a merchant who had been conducting a successful business for quite a number of years while he was the principal of the school. By the time he was taken into the Alberta government, he and Mrs. Tanner owned a chain of groceterias. Now, that is something which has been withheld, and as I say whether or not the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre knew it, I do not know. It is a point that he did not reveal.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: What has that got to do with pipe lines?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I will tell you what it has got to do with pipe lines; it has a whole lot to do with them.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I did not know it, if the hon. rqember would like to know.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: The hon. member says he did not know it.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: But I still do not think it has anything to do with the case.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: The hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre is very assiduous in hunting up a lot of things that are good for his case, but he is not so assiduous in hunting up all the facts.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: What are you doing now?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I am just pointing out the facts of the case.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I still do not know what it has to do with pipe lines.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
I will tell you what it has to do with pipe lines. When Mr. Tanner left the government of Alberta, he and Mrs. Tanner sold their chain of groceterias and invested the proceeds in the stock of Merrill oil company, and Mr. Tanner was asked to become the president and general manager of Merrill oil. For some years Mr. and Mrs. Tanner held their stock in Merrill oil and Mr. Tanner

was being paid a substantial salary as the president and general manager of an expanding company, a company whose stock began to rise on the market because of the fact they found oil on some of their property. As the Minister of Trade and Commerce (Mr. Howe) has already said, Mr. Tanner was. well on the way to an interesting and perhaps very important career as the head of one of the western oil companies. They were making some money as a consequence of wise investment.
Certainly, there is nothing wrong about that. Of course, my friends in the C.C.F. hate to see anybody making money. Now, in 1952 Mr. Tanner was asked, as I said, to become the head of this transmission company. Mr. Tanner hesitated for some years before he did consent. Finally, however, the pressure upon him to become head of the Trans-Canada Pipe Line Company increased -I know the Minister of Trade and Commerce knows that this is a fact-and the pressure on him induced him to step down from his position as president and general manager of Merrill oil. He had to liquidate his stock in that company and Mrs. Tanner did also, in order to be able to qualify as a director in the new company. Now, they put every penny they had, every dollar they had, into the new company because they wanted to make a success of it, and I know that for those two years Mr. Tanner was trying his best to get this company organized and on a firm footing. He did not know from one day to the next when every penny he and his wife had scraped together and saved-

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: What about his $35,000 salary?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Keep your big mouth quiet so I may continue. Mr. Speaker, when the man about whom I am speaking, Mr. Tanner, joined the Trans-Canada Pipe Lines Company it was nothing but a group of people who were trying to promote a pipe line transmission concern for the purpose of finding a market for Alberta gas. He and his partners put every dollar that the company owned into the original promotion. They paid for the engineering investigations; they put their money into attempts to sell gas, to try to get contracts for the purchase of gas, and all of that took a lot of money. They spent a good deal before they ever came to this parliament to ask for any assistance whatever, and it was only because of the fact that our "all-Canada policy, Canada-first policy" demanded that they build an all-Canada pipe line that it became necessary to come to the government for help.
It was because of the fact that there were certain disabilities attached to any private

company that was to yield to that policy that the government decided to come to their aid, and we agreed on both sides. But here was the important thing. These men did risk all they had, all that they could borrow somewhere, and they did not know from one day to the next whether they would ever get a penny of it back.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
How many shares did Mr. Tanner
buy?	.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Please let me say what I have to say. It does not make a bit of difference how many shares he bought. The point is, he put every penny that he and Mrs. Tanner had in the company.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, if I may interrupt, it might be well to tell the hon. members how many shares he had. Mrs. Tanner bought 10,000 shares.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: How many?

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Nine thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine shares.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: At $8 a share. The Tanner family paid some $80,000 for the shares then purchased.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Mr. Tanner bought one share at $8.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
I said, Mr. Tanner and Mrs. Tanner worked as a family unit. They did risk everything they had, and it does not matter what the amount was. They risked everything they had and when they came into Trans-Canada Pipe Lines Company, under pressure, as I said, he stepped down from a very lucrative position and a very promising future that he had in the oil company. Then, they were given inducements, and I do not blame them for one second for asking for some security in that way when they stepped down from a position such as that.
Then, I think they are entitled to some consideration. If there is anything to be made by the company, then certainly they should share equitably in what is made. Well, they did come into the company with what has been termed options. Eventually, they exercised their options. I do not know how much money they had to borrow. I imagine they had to borrow a very great sum in order to exercise the option, but in so doing they are helping the company to finance and enable it to repay to the government tomorrow afternoon what was borrowed from the government to discharge that obligation. But they are taking upon themselves right now, I imagine, the Tanners, the Coates and various others, this severe financial responsibility by way of borrowings wherever they can get
Trans-Canada Pipe Lines them to exercise those options. And if they do, in that case I certainly can see nothing wrong whatever in giving those people the chance to make some money.
I have no doubt whatever that every detail of their transactions can be laid before this parliament or any other fair judicial commission, and nothing whatsoever wrong would be found with the way they have carried on. I do deplore the innuendoes and implications that are thrown around concerning people who have been singularly successful in business, and I do not share in that attitude at all. I want to say right here, Mr. Speaker, I am satisfied that Mr. and Mrs. Tanner have conducted themselves on a high plane morally and on principle, and when they make some money I am going to be the first to rejoice, because it tells me that we are living in a country where people have made some money and the rest of us can do so also if we use our God-given right-

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Will my hon. friend permit a question?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Yes.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Will the hon. member for Peace River not admit that if Mr. and Mrs. Tanner make a large sum of money out of the dealings to which he has referred that money will be a drain on the gross national product of Canada and will reduce what is available for other people such as old age pensioners?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I think that, Mr. Speaker, is an example of about as short-circuited thinking as I have ever heard. It is absolutely typical of my hon. friends to the right.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: My hon. friend has indicated that he is concerned about old age pensioners: now I wonder.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, in the first place, let it be remembered that they have not made this money yet, and that is the only thing my hon. friend talks about. Let me make it abundantly clear, Mr. Speaker, that all that anybody can possibly say is that at the moment there is an apparent paper profit.

speakerposition: Minister of National Revenue
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Hear, hear.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
That is all, and these people over here make a tremendous thing out of an apparent paper profit. In the end, they may lose many millions of dollars as a company. Who knows? But they are risking this, and they are showing faith in their country.
Let me say one other thing. By showing initiative in risking what they have, in giving their investments, their management and their skills to the building of such a pipe line, they are making it possible to increase production in this eastern part of Canada which

Trans-Canada Pipe Lines will help to build up Canada. That is something this outfit will not look at at all. Because of their short-circuited vision they close their minds to it. I am speaking now of the C.C.F. Therefore, Mr. Speaker, I say it is about time that we got down to something like decent consideration of all the facts involved.
If there was at any time a concealment of facts which ought to be revealed in this House of Commons I do not condone it for one moment. I did not think that at the time of the pipe line debate last spring there was anything wrong with options granted to executives of the company. It is done in every organization that I know anything about and I would not be one bit surprised if a good many of my C.C.F. friends have been involved in just such transactions. I would suggest that we examine into the theatre which was built just outside Regina in which the premier of Saskatchewan was involved in a financial way. I imagine you would find some very interesting options there that were exercised.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: What has a theatre got to do with the government?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I understand there were some public moneys involved; that is, public guarantees.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Who is throwing innuendoes now?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: The one thing I am concerned about, and have been concerned about right from the beginning, is the completion of an enterprise which would just as quickly as possible provide a market for the natural gas of western Canada, particularly of Alberta, because I know it could help to strengthen the economy of Canada and it could bring back to the people of this whole country many hundreds of times any profits that any executive might make on options.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the discussion this afternoon has tended to stray some distance away from the motion that was moved by the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre, and I would point out to you, and through you to the members of the house, that the essence of the motion is contained in the last few lines. The first part of the motion sets out certain facts with regard to non-disclosure by the Minister of Trade and Commerce, and then we find these words:
.	.	. hence the need for this house to give
consideration-
And here is the subject which the motion asks the house to consider-
-to the way in which parliament and the country have been misled by not being informed as to the extent to which there would be private gain as a

result of the financial support made available to Trans-Canada Pipe Lines Limited from the public treasury.
There is the gravamen of the complaint made in this motion; and I suggest that the Minister of Trade and Commerce has made no answer whatever to that charge and of course he cannot do so, because it is only six days ago that he did mislead parliament. I have never been able to understand why he does these things, but I think under the pressure of debate he thinks of the first answer that will stop any further questioning, and he gives it; then a few days or weeks later he comes into the house and explains that he was wrong and that the real answer should have been something else. That is exactly what he did today. When the house opened he got up and said he was wrong in the answer he gave six days ago. I do not think anyone can justify actions of that kind, and the minister is quite properly being censured for having misled the house on February 19.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: It is not the first time.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: If I remember correctly I believe he also misled the house during the pipe-line debate a year ago, or in any event he did not make clear that there were these options outstanding.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: How could you make it clearer than by tabling a document that mentions the options?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I may be wrong but if I remember correctly-

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Don't give us your memory. I gave the house mine and I was wrong. Consider the possibility that you might be wrong.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I might be wrong, but I hope I would not try to get out of it by saying something that is not true. In the whole Trans-Canada Pipe Line project we have public funds being used to assist a private corporation and in effect to assist very large and powerful United States pipe-line companies which were quite able to put up all the money that was required if they had seen fit to do so.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: The good old "Texas buccaneer" cry from your party.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
The minister dragged in a red herring today by trying to compare the situation that obtained in relation to Trans-Canada Pipe Lines Limited with that of Westcoast Transmission Company Limited. The minister knows and I think we all realize that Westcoast is entirely a private company,

building its line and doing all its work without any government assistance. The situation with regard to Westcoast Transmission Company Limited is vastly different from that of the Trans-Canada Pipe Lines Limited, which was able to get from the government an agreement to loan $80 million for building the easiest part of the line, which was supposed to have been finished last year but which of course was not finished. In that regard there was another instance of the minister misleading the house. He told the house last year that Trans-Canada Pipe Lines Limited had pipe rolled and ready-

speakerposition: Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Defence Production
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: No, he did not.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: -to be brought to Canada.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Defence Production
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: He never said anything of the kind.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: That was never said by me, and my hon. friend is now trying to mislead the house. He is not being very successful, however, because everyone knows better.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: It is my information that they did not have the pipe rolled at all.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: No one ever said they did have the pipe rolled.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Defence Production
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: No one said they had.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: In addition to the loan of $80 million the governments are building the most difficult part of the pipe line from the Manitoba-Ontario boundary to Kapuskasing at a cost to the taxpayers of $117 million, and so this case is completely different from that of Westcoast Transmission Company Limited. The house and the people of Canada are entitled to an absolutely honest statement of all the facts in connection with this transaction.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Well, they will never get it from you.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
I hope that in future the minister will not be in such a rush to put things on the record in order to stop criticism, with the result that we have to learn in other ways that he has not been giving the proper facts.
It is material that these options were not exercised until about two weeks ago. They were exercised after the board of transport commissioners had made an order on January 31, 1957, giving the company the right to go ahead; and in making that order someone had appeared on behalf of the Minister of Trade and Commerce to urge that the order be made. It is not as though Mr. Tanner and Mr. Coates had exercised these options when there was the slightest risk. On the 82715-103
Trans-Canada Pipe Lines contrary they waited until after the order had been made by the board of transport commissioners and then exercised the options, and no one can deny that they are in a position to make large sums of money as a result.
I suggest that there should not have been any arrangement of this kind in the first place where the government and the country were involved. There should not have been the provision for these options under which the officers of the company could make profits. After all these gentlemen are not taking a great deal of chance in working for Trans-Canada Pipe Lines Limited. Mr. Tanner is receiving an annual salary of $35,000, I believe, which is guaranteed until 1959 or 1960, as I understand it, and Mr. Coates is receiving a salary of $45,000. These men really do not need much sympathy, and I do not believe they are asking for any, because they were well taken care of in the provision made for their salaries.
The whole attitude of the minister on this question is really fantastic. For one thing he has tried to allege that the Conservative party was against a Canada first pipe line.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Well, was I
mistaken? What was all the debate about during the last session, a debate that lasted for approximately six weeks?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: That related to closure:

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: It did not indicate that you and your associates were in favour of the pipe line.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
It has nothing to do with
whether or not the Conservative party favoured a Canada first policy. Most of that debate was taken up by the question of closure. Practically all the time was spent in protesting the use of closure by the government, and very little time was left for discussing the pipe-line question at all.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Defence Production
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Because you did not want
to discuss the pipe line.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
As far as the pipe line was
concerned the main points in the debate related to the manner in which the government was stepping in to finance these great United States pipe-line corporations in the construction of the pipe line.
When Mr. Murchison first came and obtained a charter he was prepared to build that line from Alberta to Montreal and he was prepared to build it with his own money in just the same way the Westcoast Transmission Company Limited is building a line from the Peace river district down to Vancouver.

Trans-Canada Pipe Lines
Another pipe-line group, Western Pipe Lines I think it was, came into the picture and eventually we ended up with a company largely controlled by Tennessee Gas Transmission. As the minister knows, those were the main points of the debate a year ago.
We have been pressing the minister for years to adopt a Canada first policy with regard to these gas pipe lines. It will be remembered that back in 1950 we urged that the pipe line to the west coast should go from the Peace river down through British Columbia rather than from southern Alberta into southeastern British Columbia and then down into the United States.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: With ninety per cent of the gas going into the United States.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Yes, but the people of Canada are being served first. In 1950 the minister and the Prime Minister threw all their weight behind the proposal that gas to the west coast should go via a United States route. The only reason we spoke in favour of the McMahon plan for Westcoast Transmission Company Limited was that he proposed to bring gas from the Peace river right down through British Columbia serving practically every community in that province.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I suggest that my hon. friend is now deceiving the house. He cannot document a single statement he has made.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: I could quote-

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Please do.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: -from those debates by the page.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Go ahead.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Hon. members who were here at that time know that is what all the fighting on the pipe-line charters was about, trying to force a Canada first policy. Some of the minister's own supporters, the former member for Fraser Valley, George Cruick-shank; the former member for Comox-Alberni, Jack Gibson, and several others of the minister's supporters fought with us to force a Canada first policy. Eventually we were successful with regard to gas going to the west coast, and we have been successful with regard to gas to eastern Ontario.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Are you the man
who built the pipe line?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: The minister did not favour that policy for a long time.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: The minister does not like to hear the true facts in this pipe-line business. He has built up a mythology about it with which he wants people to agree.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
The minister will remember that three days before he announced his Canada first policy the then leader of the opposition, Hon. Mr. Drew, made a very strong speech on the question in which he said:
Let the government declare that the first Interest to be served will be the interests of the Canadian people-a Canada first policy in the use of these resources.
Several days later the minister came out with the same policy. He will remember that on several occasions during subsequent debates I pointed out that he had at last got on the same side as myself and he replied, "Well, that worries me; I am afraid I must be wrong." When he comes into this house and alleges that the Conservative party was opposed to a Canada first policy he is distorting the facts and misleading the house more than he did in the answers he made last week.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Once again the hon. member is distorting the facts. I said that during last year's debate, that the Conservative party was opposing the pipe line; I did not say they were opposing the Canada first principle of a pipe line.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: You mean during the debate last year?

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: At that time we were opposing the way in which the minister was proposing to do it.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: There are several ways of carrying out a pipe-line project within Canada.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: You were opposing the pipe line.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
To come back to the motion before the house today, no matter how the minister may twist and turn he cannot get away from the facts. This motion sets out the actual fact that he did mislead the house last week. After having been some 22 years in parliament, during all of which time he has been a minister of the crown, surely we have reached the stage that when this senior minister gets up and makes a statement we should be able to rely upon his stating actual facts. It makes a farce of parliament when a leading minister does this thing time and time again, gets up in the house and gives replies that are inaccurate. How can parliament function when there is that little responsibility in the mind of this particular minister for giving parliament the facts?
When we vote on this motion, that is the question on which we shall be voting, whether or not this minister has mislead the house on this particular occasion. I suggest

that no matter how the vote may go in this house the fact that the house has been misled cannot be gainsaid.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, in rising to speak on this motion I want to say I have listened most carefully to the remarks of the Minister of Trade and Commerce, and of the hon. member for Peace River. I was very interested in listening to the remarks of the hon. member for Peace River, the leader in this house of the Social Credit group. The man is positively amazing in the way in which he can evade the question and build up a red herring. I almost had tears in my eyes as I listened to his long harangue, his long Horatio Alger story of Mr. Tanner, rising from a poor boy to a teacher and then to the position which he now occupies executively and financially.
I am quite certain that many of us were almost overcome when we were told that this man had been pressured into taking his present position, that he had been pressured into taking a position having a salary of $35,000 a year for five years, or a total of $175,000. He is now half way through his term, and if he should retire he will receive $15,000 a year extra, or a total of $75,000. He was pressured into taking a job which in five years will pay him $175,000, and which in ten years, if he retires after five years, will represent a total of $250,000.
Then he was given the right to purchase
60,000	shares at $2 less than the stock market value. It was most interesting to hear the hon. member for Peace River tell us how this Horatio Alger chap had sacrificed his all to take this job to the extent that he invested the sum of $8 to purchase one share. His wife purchased 9,999 shares at a cost of $79,992.
I think my hon. friend is making a mistake. He should have given the credit to Mr. Tanner's wife, not to Mr. Tanner. He only had a confidence amounting to $8.
However, it is interesting to note the type of speech made by hon. members of the Social Credit group, and I would suggest through you, sir, to the supporters of the Liberal party that before they applaud so heartily when they think they hear something against the motion now before this house, they should give consideration to the economics of the situation in Canada. That applies in particular to the supporters of Social Credit who have been weeping so many crocodile tears about the plight of old age pensioners and veterans, and who have even gone so far as to oppose the distribution of grants under the Canada Council because they felt increases in pensions ought to come 82715-103i
Trans-Canada Pipe Lines first. Yet on an issue which concerns hundreds of millions of dollars, the money being made by racketeers, they think it is quite all right for them to make the money on the stock market, not realizing that, on an economic basis, this is a completely unearned increment and, as such, has to come out of the finances of this country and is therefore not available to be used on services such as pensions.

speakerposition: Minister of Citizenship and Immigration
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Is this the new line?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
I have never in my life heard such economic stupidity as we have heard from the hon. members on my left in the Social Credit group. As a matter of fact, the very situation we are now discussing is one of the major reasons why inflation exits in this country and one of the major reasons why money is not now available for the necessities that are required by our people with regard to housing and with regard to pensions, in particular.
I was most disappointed in the remarks of the Minister of Trade and Commerce. I have known the minister by reputation since I was 17 years of age, and I have known him personally since I came here after the election in 1953. But, sir, on an issue as important as the one we are now discussing it was a bit of a let-down to hear the minister mainly concerned open up by trying to becloud the issue completely. That is what he was trying to do in his opening sentences, by holding up the Prime Minister and saying that nobody could match his record.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: Hear, hear.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
There, you see, is the empty-headedness of hon. members on the government side. Their brains are in their hands instead of being in their heads. I say that because those opening remarks of the Minister of Trade and Commerce were directly, or perhaps indirectly, an insult to every hon. member of this house. Over the years only one person can be Prime Minister but, Mr. Speaker, every hon. member of this house has responsibility, and I take it they are sincere in discharging those responsibilities. And in doing their jobs their reputations, as such, on the floor of parliament are just as good as that of the Prime Minister. I certainly say that as far as I am concerned, because the minister said, "I challenge any man to stand up and say he can meet the record of the Prime Minister." As hon. members of the House of Commons all of us can, because that is our responsibility. Only one person can be Prime Minister, but you can be for 24 years, Mr. Speaker, a member of parliament and 12 years leader of the opposition, doing your job and doing it well in the public's

Trans-Canada Pipe Lines estimation. So I think it was very unfair of the Minister of Trade and Commerce to try to raise the matter on the basis he did.
He followed these remarks not by discussing the issue that is now before us but by saying that something even worse has been done, mentioning Mr. Frank McMahon and Westcoast Transmission. We agree that what he spoke of has occurred. There is no question about that. That is why, Mr. Speaker, -and the minister's words have given added impetus to our conviction in the C.C.F. group -we say there should be an investment control board under the authority of an act of the House of Commons, and that is why there should be a capital gains tax so as to prevent that kind of financial racketeer increasing his ' income to an unnecessarily high basis.
Mr. Speaker, I would point this out and it is something which was not pointed out by the Minister of Trade and Commerce, namely that the Westcoast Transmission Company, despite all that has been said about it, was not a company that could not get started unless it had the backing of the finances of the federal government. That, in my estimation, is a great differentiation between the instance which the minister gave and the situation that we are discussing today.
Speaking about this stock business, the Minister of Trade and Commerce made this statement with regard to Mr. Tanner and Mr. Coates; I wrote it down at the time; "So it is only a natural thing in such an organization, and it is only money." I wrote it down and he said it. He said, "It is only money". But, Mr. Speaker, money means nothing unless it has value, and the value of money lies in what you can exchange it for-in the last analysis, consumer goods. So what he says is "only money" is taking away a great deal from the natural flow of money in Canada and has, therefore, a great effect on inflation through money unearned by people who benefit through a very peculiar stock manipulation.
The Minister of Trade and Commerce said that in our discussion we were bickering. Mr. Speaker, I can assure you that it is not a question of bickering at all. This, in my humble estimation, is one of the most important questions that has ever come up on the floor of the House of Commons; that is, that the proof is now conclusive that the House of Commons was misled with regard to the bill introduced last year, the bill that was forced through by a method unknown in any democratic parliament in the commonwealth of nations, and the contentions which were made by hon. members of two parties of the opposition a year ago have now been 

proven to be correct. It has taken approximately ten months, but after ten months the truth is now out that a bill was foisted on the parliament of this country and, therefore, on the people of Canada with regard to which all information was not given. This information was known to at least one cabinet minister and, undoubtedly, to others; and because the information was not made known and the evidence was withheld, we now have what is tantamount to a conspiracy between the government and private enterprise for fortunes to be made by a private enterprise company.
We must recognize-and it is important that we should do so, irrespective of the red herrings that the government and the "socreds" try to bring up on this picture- that Trans-Canada Pipe Lines could not have gone through and would not have gone through unless they could reach an agreement with the federal government. They could not finance. The federal government decided, in conjunction with the Ontario government, to finance a non-profitable line in a certain part of Ontario, something that is going to cost the federal government at least $80 million. But even at that this company could not finance the balance of their line.
Therefore without any question of doubt whatesover it was an arrangement whereby, by the use of the taxpayers' money, with this guarantee, a private company was to be put in a position in which it could then raise the money; the government could withdraw, and the private enterprise could make its millions to its heart's content. Not only could the company make millions to its heart's content but it is now obvious that the government knew- I will not say they conspired with them but they acquiesced-that two individuals in that company could make unwarranted profits out of stock market manipulation, because they could buy at less than the stock market price.
Surely, Mr. Speaker, we on this side of the house are in duty bound to face our responsibility to draw to the attention of the members of this house and of the people of Canada the despicable, low-down sell-out of parliament and of the people in the introduction of the bill last year in the way in which it was done, the way in which it was carried through, and the effect of it. Here I am going to say to the government that if they did not know this could happen, they have the power now to do something about it and we are asking them to do it. If they plead "not guilty" with regard to what happened last session, then they should prove it by taking action now at this session-this week, as a matter of fact-to see that this

unwarranted profit of the company is stopped; and I include the two executives who are involved.
As has already been pointed out, if a situation like this had even been rumoured in the House of Commons at Westminster, not only would a minister have resigned but, on such an occurrence, the government would have resigned, because it is without a doubt a betrayal of democracy and a betrayal of cabinet responsibility to parliament and to the people. Mr. Speaker, all you have to do is to go over the record of ten months ago and go over the record as it is now. I refer to the stock market record, the information in the press and the statements made in this House of Commons. Surely, Mr. Speaker, there should be a deep recognition of the fact that if this situation is allowed to continue without correction, it will be the biggest black eye ever given a democratic parliament in the history of the British commonwealth. Because the Prime Minister is Prime Minister, he must bear the major responsibility.
I can do no more than just say this. I do not say it because I am a member of the opposition, but I say it because over a period of 24 years I have come to have a love and an understanding of the meaning of parliament and of the responsibilities of members of parliament and of the cabinet. Because of that fact, and because of my respect for parliament and all it means and has meant over the centuries and because of my love for this country I appeal through you, Mr. Speaker, to the Prime Minister. Tough as it may be for him to recognize that a mistake has been made or to admit that a mistake has been made, I appeal to him to take the necessary corrective action. I can assure you, Mr. Speaker, that I will be the first man to stand in my place and applaud him if he has the integrity, the sincerity and the courage so to do.

Trans-Canada Pipe Lines

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Naturally I bow to your wishes, but I simply mentioned that fact as an example of the design and pattern which has been developed recently in this house by the Minister of Trade and Commerce, who is making a very definite habit of misleading the house.
In his remarks a few minutes ago the Minister of Trade and Commerce spoke almost pathetically of the four years of great anxiety that were suffered by Mr. Tanner and Mr. Coates, as well as the other senior officials of Trans-Canada Pipe Lines. I never heard anything in my life that contained so much tommyrot. Anxiety for what? Was there anxiety over the fact that the shares might go down? Of course not; the shares were not going to go down. They did not have to take up their options until they were positive the shares would go up, and go up materially.
Was there anxiety over the fact that the bill would not pass? Of course not; they knew quite well that this government, with its dictatorial methods, would jam down the throat of parliament, by the use of closure, a bill which they had no right to have passed by this house. There was no anxiety there. Was there anxiety over the finances which Trans-Canada Pipe Lines was so anxious to obtain from the federal government? Of course not; it was quite obvious right from the start that the Minister of Trade and Commerce had given assurances to the officers of Trans-Canada that whatever they wanted in the way of financing or building would be made available to them. All they had to do was snap their fingers. They had the Minister of Trade and Commerce wrapped around their little finger, and they knew it. There was no anxiety whatever. This story about anxiety was really a comic piece which the Minister of Trade and Commerce introduced into this serious debate this afternoon.
From 1951 on, as we all know, this company came before the board of transport commissioners and gave unqualified assurances that this line would be built without any assistance from the public treasury. Then in August, 1955, they cried on the minister's shoulder and got the northern Ontario section built. Then in the fall of last year they had the prairie section financed for them. This whole enterprise, Mr. Speaker, has been made nothing more nor less than an investors' paradise. This line was an enterprise in which there was no risk taken by the company, and all the risks and financing that were required were put up by the people of Canada. According to the reports of the past few days, Mr. Tanner and Mr. Coates have already made paper profits of approximately half a million dollars each. This has been the story throughout this whole sordid procedure.
[The Acting Speaker (Mr. Applewhaite).]
Last year, Mr. Speaker, I said that from the favours which this company was receiving from this government it would be very surprising if at least a million dollars did not find its way into the campaign funds of the Liberal party for this campaign.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, so far the debate on this motion has indicated quite clearly that it would be impossible to separate the immediate issues from the general question of the relationship between Trans-Canada Pipe Lines and the government. It seems now that there are two bases for this issue, that is a moral and an economic issue.
In the first place we have the position before us that the government has, not only on this occasion but on previous occasions in connection with this whole Trans-Canada Pipe Line question, misled the house and the committee a number of times. The situation is that the Minister of Trade and Commerce found it convenient to rise today and make an apology for having misled the house a week ago. It may be only a coincidence but if so it is a rather striking coincidence, that he chose this particular time to do it. I have great respect for the officials of his department, and I cannot believe it took them a whole week to find out that the minister had made an error.
It may only be coincidence that it was only after the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre took it upon himself as a public duty to make a certain investigation and had obtained certain information which, by the very nature of it, had to come from the minister's department, that the minister found it convenient to rise and make his apology. This in itself is a rather serious situation because what would have been the

case had the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre not been as alert as he usually is, and had he not gone to the trouble of making this investigation into the facts disclosing these misleading statements? It is quite possible that this apology would never have been made at all. The minister might have been quite prepared to let the matter slide and let that inaccurate reply join all the others that have been made over the years.
In doing this I think the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre has performed a public service. It is the kind of thing which makes parliament effective, the kind of thing which makes democracy effective, when each member of this house takes it upon himself to make sure that the information given to the house and by that method to the public, is accurate information based upon the facts; in other words that it is the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Parliament would be that much stronger and democracy that much more effective if more of that kind of work were done in parliament. I feel, therefore, that the hon. member deserves the commendation of this house and of the public for having been effective as he has been in the past, in disclosing inaccuracies, whether they be inaccuracies caused by neglect or lack of memory or whether they be done for a purpose.
In reply to the motion the Minister of Trade and Commerce made a certain statement which in my opinion, raised some very important questions. He started off by making the amazing statement that you cannot build a pipe line with money; you must have brains. What does that mean? What is the implication of that? The implication, as I see it, is that the minister is abdicating the responsibility he has in this house, the responsibility he has to this country.
During the years of the war the same minister did not seem to have much difficulty in finding the brains to set up some of the finest national enterprises that we have in this country. He did not seem to find it difficult to locate the brains to establish the synthetic rubber plant known as the Polymer plant and many other enterprises such as the Trans-Canada Air Lines. Parliament was able to find the brains to conduct a utility such as the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation and a great many other publicly-owned utilities, which are giving this country great service and performing them at cost, and which are not there to provide a profit for any private individual or firm but to provide a service at cost. And then, all of a sudden, when we come to a pipe-line bill the minister gives up in despair and tells us that
Trans-Canada Pipe Lines all the brains he can lay his hands on, or that the government or parliament can lay its hands on, have been exhausted. Now they must go to a private company and finance this company because somebody in that company has all the brains with regard to the transmission of gas. What an argument.
If Mr. Tanner and Mr. Coates, or any combination of experts having anything to do with this company, had such qualifications as have been described and had been prepared to go to private sources to obtain the financing, then this parliament would not have been concerned with the matter. But the fact that the officials of this company came to this government and to this parliament and asked the public purse of Canada to take the risk indicates that they themselves did not have nearly as much confidence in themselves, or in their ability to organize the company, as the Minister of Trade and Commerce gave them credit for.
Perhaps the most serious implication in the minister's statement is that it strikes a blow directly at national enterprise. I was amazed and somewhat shocked to hear that in practically the same sentence he said-[DOT] referring to Mr. Tanner-that here was a man who was prepared to take the leadership of a great national enterprise. He referred again and again to Trans-Canada Pipe Lines as a national enterprise. Well, it is nothing of the sort.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Don't misquote the
minister.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
The words of the minister are on the record, and if I misquote him he will be well within his rights to correct me. I took the words down, and he referred to Trans-Canada Pipe Lines as a national enterprise.
Is it not a complete abdication of responsibility when this nation of ours, capable of doing what it was able to do in the second world war, capable of doing what it has been able to do through national enterprises since the war, all of a sudden folds up and has to term a private monopoly a national enterprise, has to hang the tag or the label of national enterprise on a privately-owned monopoly, the majority of which is owned by interests outside of our nation, in order to have an excuse to put some public funds into something which is not ours and which never will be ours under the present set-up? By saying that the minister admitted that if we are interested as a parliament, and if the government is interested in national enterprise as such, then what the government should have done was create a national

Trans-Canada Pipe Lines enterprise in 1951, when the charter was granted to the pipe-line company to build a pipe line.
That was the stage at which the minister would have been quite within his rights-and this parliament had a public duty to perform -in creating a national enterprise. If he had done that we would have had the pipe line built and functioning and carrying gas as far as Montreal by now. We would not be sitting around arguing as to when they are going to get as far as Winnipeg, or when they are going to get as far as Montreal. What excuse has the company for the delays which seem to be bedevilling the whole situation?
Had the government and this parliament taken the steps that this nation demanded of them they would have started back in 1950 or 1951 as a national enterprise, and we would have had today a trans-Canada gas line functioning and providing a service at cost to the Canadian people. But the government did otherwise. They decided to place public money into a private monopoly.
Let me refer again to the two gentlemen who have been the subject of discussion today, namely Mr. Tanner and Mr. Coates. I wish to make it quite clear, Mr. Speaker, that I do not desire to say anything about these gentlemen, or any others, which will damage their reputations or take away from them anything they have accomplished. I have never made it a habit to attack anyone's character in a matter of this kind. Therefore the whole question of whether or not Mr. Tanner by his efforts or by his brilliancy reached the position he has is beside the question. No one is attacking Mr. Tanner.

speakerposition: Minister of Transport

speechtext:
Just the Leader of the
Opposition.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
If someone else used it he must have had a good reason for using the term. 1 am making it clear that the issue before us is not the character of Mr. Tanner, Mr. Coates or anyone else; it is the question of whether the government and this parliament were within their rights to finance a privately-owned company which happens to occupy a monopolistic position and to put these gentlemen, or any other gentlemen, in


the position of being able to profit individually and privately as a result of the public purse participating in the venture. That is the whole question.
If I may, I should like to refer to an editorial which appeared in the Toronto Telegram on February 22, which sets out the situation rather clearly. They put it in these words:
The issue of shares to management is a common practice in private companies, and on that basis Right Hon. C. D. Howe defended the Trans-Canada transactions involving senior officers. The fact remains that substantial private profits have accrued to individuals as a result mainly of governmental help for a company that pleaded inability to carry out its project without it. This is a situation that does nothing to create confidence in the manner in which governments have entered into the pipe line project.
The most serious criticism of the Trans-Canada deal is that, with the original risk capital put up by the taxpayers, the company and not the taxpayers will harvest the profits.
This is a forthright statement in an editorial in a newspaper which I think even the government on occasion has quoted in setting up some of its arguments, and that I think is the nub of the whole situation. That is why I felt almost a year ago, or the first time I spoke on this matter, that it would be a tragic mistake on the part of this parliament and on the part of this government to allow public funds to be used for the purpose of creating a private monopoly.
If we wish to go back to the beginning it must be remembered, Mr. Speaker, that it was the Minister of Trade and Commerce himself who on one occasion rose in this very house and announced that he had been instrumental in bringing together three pipeline companies and having them merged into what is now known as Trans-Canada Pipe Lines. If I remember correctly he said it was in his office that the conversations were held that resulted in this merger.
Referring to that almost a year ago, I made a statement which I think has been borne out by events. I said that the minister came very close to violating the Combines Investigations Act by taking part in the formation of a combine. Certainly it should not be the function of a minister of the crown to be a party to the formation of combines in this country, or the formation of monopolies, for the purpose of exploiting the consumers of this country, and that is exactly what was done.
That is where I think the minister made his fatal mistake, because at that time he had a choice of either going ahead with this project as a public enterprise, or as he himself calls it a national enterprise-and then it would have been a truly national enterprise instead of the phony national enterprise it is now- or he could have completely washed his hands
162S

of the thing and said, "All right, we will leave it to free enterprise and let those fellows do it on their own, and if they want to form a merger or go to the United States to get their capital, that is their business and we as the government will have nothing to do with it." But he took neither one choice nor the other. Instead he took the steps which helped to form this merger which in turn created this monopoly, this Frankenstein which now has its tentacles in the consumer's pocket, and this is only the beginning.
Then in order to add insult to injury as far as the taxpayer is concerned, after having made sure the consumer was going to have one pocket picked by this company through the forming of a monopoly, he stuck his hand into the other pocket as well and took out some of the taxpayer's money and gave it to this company and said, "Here is some money to make it easier for you to form this monopoly."
That is the kind of thing to which I have objected and to which I shall continue to object as long as I am in this parliament. I have done a little tabulating, and I find that the tax money of the people of my constituency was filched to the extent of about $500,000. This amount of money was taken from the people I represent by this government in order to provide this privately-owned company with an opportunity to set up a huge monopoly across the country which will exploit the very people who helped to finance it. Is that the kind of transaction to which the Minister of Trade and Commerce should be a party? That is the chain of events which put the government in the trouble they are in now.
Another statement the minister made which I think has very serious implications is this. If I heard him correctly, he said that sometime tomorrow afternoon he expects that Trans-Canada Pipe Lines will come along with a cheque for $80 million plus interest and place it in his hands, and then he concluded by saying that from then on as far as he is concerned it will be free enterprise, the government will have nothing further to do with it, and they will not answer questions about this company. He suggested that they would simply say that the information is in the hands of the company and that the government is not concerned.
Surely the minister does not think he can get away with that kind of statement. Over $100 million of the taxpayers' money is still involved in this business. The minister attempted to brush off the question of the northern Ontario section of the pipe line by saying that it has nothing to do with Trans-Canada Pipe Lines but is rather a joint project between the federal government and
Trans-Canada Pipe Lines the government of Ontario. Well, technically so far this may be so; but the very basis upon which that crown company was created in order to build that pipe line is contained in the agreement to which it is attached, which states very plainly that the purpose of setting up that crown corporation to build the northern Ontario section of the pipe line was so that immediately upon its completion it must be leased to Trans-Canada Pipe Lines which would have an option to buy it at any time they wished. What is more, the company is under no obligation to buy it at any time. In other words, they have it all their own way.
The agreement under which the pipe line is leased to the company for a period of 25 years is part and parcel of the whole thing. The sum of over $100 million is involved in that transaction; yet the minister stood up in this house and said that tomorrow after he receives a cheque for $80 million, as far as he is concerned it is a free enterprise from that point on.
That in itself is misleading the public to the nth degree, because the public treasury is involved in this entire pipe-line deal and will remain involved until the whole pipe line has been completed, and until such time as it suits the company to take complete ownership of the pipe line from Alberta right through to Montreal. They will only do that upon their own terms, and only if it appears to them to be the best thing to do. This government are not going to be able to shrug themselves away from the deal into which they have gotten themselves as easily as they think.
It is for this reason that I think the hon. member for Vancouver East was right on the beam when he made the plea that it is not too late even yet for this government to salvage something from this whole unhappy business for the Canadian public. It is not too late for this parliament to decide once and for all to end this miserable business and take the steps that need to be taken. It is not too late for the government to swallow its pride and admit its mistake and let this parliament make the move and take over the entire Trans-Canada Pipe Line project as a publicly-owned project to be handled for the benefit of the consumers of Canada, to provide a service at cost. Then the public of Canada will know in what their money is invested. If this is done they will then know that this is truly a national enterprise owned by the citizens of Canada and not by foreign interests, built to serve the citizens of Canada and not for the gain of a few private individuals.

speechtext: think that stands particularly true when those who receive such rewards appear to have little to recommend them except a past political affiliation or perhaps even a present political affiliation. Both the Minister of Trade and Commerce and the leader of the Social Credit party made a great stand this afternoon on behalf of Messrs. Coates and Tanner. The Minister of Trade and Commerce presented these gentlemen as if they had almost single-handed made possible the development of the Trans-Canada Pipe Lines.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: The gold dust twins.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
The
leader of the Social Credit party particularly came to the defence of Mr. Tanner. He was a great Canadian who had suffered tremendously in order to enter this Trans-Canada Pipe Lines operation. He had endangered everything he had built up over the years in order to do this. Those were the remarks of the leader of the Social Credit party.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext: You are allowing your imagination to run wild.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA PIPE LINES ALLEGED MISLEADING OF PARLIAMENT    MOTION FOR ADJOURNMENT UNDER STANDING ORDER 26
speechtext:
Fortunately we have a Hansard in this house and those remarks can be checked. I made notes as the leader of the Social Credit party went along. Then the Minister of Trade and Commerce, referring I think specifically to Mr. Tanner, remarked that we do not build these things with money alone, that you must have brainpower. He pointed out that it was this brainpower which Mr. Tanner had brought to Trans-Canada which has merited this rather substantial allotment of shares under an option arrangement with him.
Let us for a moment examine the record of Mr. Tanner in order to see what brainpower he brought to this particular project. In the first instance the implication of the leader of the Social Credit party that Mr. Tanner had long been absent from the provincial government before he entered the affairs of Trans-Canada Pipe Lines is simply wrong. Mr. Tanner remained in the Social Credit cabinet of the province of Alberta until August, 1952. There is a slight overlapping, which is interesting to note, between the original developments leading to the creation of Trans-Canada Pipe Lines and Mr. Tanner's membership in the Alberta government.
Then Mr. Tanner left and went with Merrill Petroleums Limited, which is an Alberta company. The next apparent oversight on the part of the leader of the Social Credit party was his implication that when Mr. Tanner joined Trans-Canada Pipe Lines it was necessary for him to remove himself from Merrill Petroleums. I want to say he did not do that. The implication that Tanner was sacrificing something he had built up over the years was quite wrong. His interest in this corporation with which he, according to the leader of the Social Credit party, had been associated for so many years and had helped to build up was not long.
I hold in my hand the 1956 "Survey of Oils" published by the Financial Post which lists Mr. Tanner as chairman of Merrill Petroleums Limited. There was a change- this is important because of what I am going to say-in Mr. Tanner's position with this company. From the time he left the Social Credit cabinet to enter this company that had dealings with the Social Credit government he was president of Merrill Petroleums. As we all know that meant he was the operating head of the company, the man who was primarily responsible for the day-to-day activities.
When he joined Trans-Canada he resigned his presidency and moved upward as chairman of the board, where he lost contact with

the day to day operations of Merrill Petroleums. However, he still retained his interest and presided at directors' meetings. I suggest that was the best thing in the world that ever happened to Merrill Petroleums. Let me tell you what this great brainpower Which was emphasized so much by the Minister of Trade and Commerce in connection with this man actually did.

While Mr. Tanner was president, with this great brainpower of his, Merrill Petroleums was losing money hand over fist. However, as I pointed out, the move upward or perhaps the kick upward to chairman of the board, a position in which he was no longer the operating head, mirabilus dictu, which, if I may translate for the benefit of the Minister of Trade and Commerce, means marvellous to say-

Because, as I said in the beginning-

As one who believes that the government must be founded on two things, first of all the personal respect of members of the cabinet for the House of Commons and its right to information and, secondly, the personal integrity of every member who sits in any legislature in Canada, I find these events, Mr. Speaker, a cause of great disappointment and dismay.
